Q. 
Please explain how the corrections and updates are organized. 
9 
A. 
The exhibits submitted in this filing show corrections and/or updates and 
10 
indicate the change from the original filing.  The exhibits are labeled with “CU” 
11 
after the original label.  For example, Exhibit __ (RRP-1) in the April 28 filing 
12 
is the Statement of Operating Income.  The exhibit showing the corrections 
13 
and/or updates to the Statement of Operating Income is labeled Exhibit ___ 
14 
(RRP-1CU).  The first page of each exhibit provides a summary of all 
15 
adjustments made and reflected in that exhibit.  This summary, or lead page, is 
16 
identified as “Corrections and Updates” under each exhibit number.  The 
17 
revised schedules and pages supporting each exhibit correspond to the 
18 
schedules and pages originally filed.  The Company has only included exhibits, 
19 
summaries, schedules, and pages where corrections and/or updates were made, 
20 


--- Page 5 ---
 
Corrections and Updates Testimony of The Revenue Requirements Panel 
Page 3 of 30 
 
except for in the case of Exhibit___(RRP-3CU), where all schedules are being 
1 
included. 
2 
 
3 
The information requests referenced in the Panel’s testimony are all included in   
4 
Exhibit ___ (RRP-12CU) in alphanumeric order.   In the specific exhibits and 
5 
schedules where the corrections and/or updates were made, the testimony will 
6 
reference the specific information request.  For example, if a correction and/or 
7 
update is shown in Exhibit ___ (RRP-3CU), Schedule 2 based on a response to 
8 
an 
information 
request, 
that 
information 
request 
is 
included 
in 
9 
Exhibit____(RRP-12CU).  Where the attachments to information requests are 
10 
voluminous, the Company included only the written response and relevant 
11 
attachments.

requirement in this proceeding? 
15

16 
million greater than revenue at present rates.  The corrections and updates 
17 
increase the Company’s revenue requirement for the Rate Year by $35.9 
18 
million, to $450.1 million, as shown in Exhibit ___ (RRP-1CU), Page 1, and 
19 
the table below.

1 
Q. 
What are the primary corrections and/or updates affecting the revenue 
2 
requirement in the Rate Year? 
3 
A. 
The primary corrections and/or updates affecting the revenue requirement in 
4 
the Rate Year are (i) an update to the Company’s revenue forecast that 
5 
decreased gas sales revenues, (ii) updates and corrections that increased 
6 
KEDNY’s excess earnings base adjustment partially offset by an accumulated 
7 
deferred tax credit included in rate base, (iii) increased property taxes, and (iv) 
8 
corrections and updates that collectively reduced the Company’s O&M 
9 
expense.

6

Federal and State Income Taxes 
12 
Q. 
Has the Company made any corrections or updates to federal and state 
13 
income tax expense? 
14 
A. 
Yes, the Company made adjustments to reflect changes to the amortization of 
15 
excess accumulated deferred income tax (“ADIT”) to reflect the impact of the 
16 
extension of the temporary New York State (“NYS”) tax rate increase of 7.25 
17 
percent through Data Year 3, and to reflect the flow through effect of changes 
18 
in the revenue requirement and rate base on income tax expense, as shown in 
19 
Exhibit ____(RRP-6CU). 
20

--- Page 22 ---
 
Corrections and Updates Testimony of The Revenue Requirements Panel 
Page 20 of 30 
 
Q. 
Please describe the change to the amortization of excess ADIT. 
1 
A. 
The Company adjusted the balance of the overall excess ADIT to reflect 
2 
adjustments stemming from the settlements of the federal income tax audits for 
3 
the periods ended March 31, 2010 through March 31, 2018.  For the temporary 
4 
audit adjustments agreed to in the settlements with the Internal Revenue Service 
5 
(“IRS”), the current taxes were recorded at a 35 percent tax rate (the tax rate in 
6 
effect for the years under audit), but the deferred taxes were recorded at a 21 
7 
percent tax rate (the tax rate in effect for the years ended after March 31, 2018). 
8 
The resulting difference in the applicable tax rates increased the regulatory 
9 
liability for excess ADIT.  The Company applied amortization lives adopted in 
10 
the 2019 KEDNY and KEDLI Rate Cases to the adjusted excess ADIT 
11 
numbers, which changed the excess ADIT amortization amounts in the Rate 
12 
Year through Data Year 3. 
13 
 
14 
Q. 
Please describe the impact of the extension of the increased NYS tax rate. 
15 
A. 
On May 3, 2023, NYS enacted legislation that extends the expiration dates of 
16 
the increased corporate tax rate and business capital base tax.  The legislation 
17 
extends the 7.25 percent corporate tax rate and the 0.1875 percent business 
18 
capital base tax for an additional three years, through tax year 2026, which for 
19 
the Company is FY 2027.  The extension of the higher tax rate increases income 
20 
tax expense in the Rate Year through Data Year 2.  Additionally, the extension 
21 


--- Page 23 ---
 
Corrections and Updates Testimony of The Revenue Requirements Panel 
Page 21 of 30 
 
of the higher tax rate extends the period in which excess or deficient 
1 
accumulated deferred state income tax (“excess ADSIT” or “deficient 
2 
ADSIT”), which gives rise to a tax regulatory liability or asset, may originate.  
3 
Because the final amount of the excess or deficient ADSIT cannot be 
4 
determined at this time, the Company removed the amortization of excess 
5 
ADSIT for the period April 1, 2021 through March 31, 2022 from the 
6 
calculation of the income tax expense in the Rate Year set forth in the “NYS & 
7 
MTA Tax Rate Change 2021” line item in the Company’s April 28 filing, as 
8 
described in response to Information Request No. DPS-424. 
9

B. 
Deferred Taxes 
1 
Q. 
Please describe the changes made to the deferred tax forecasts, as shown 
2 
in Exhibit ___ (RRP-7CU), Schedule 3. 
3 
A. 
 The Company made changes to the deferred tax forecast to reflect (i) the 
4 
updated ADIT balances from December 31, 2022 to March 31, 2023, (ii) the 
5 
impact of the revenue requirement increase on net operating loss (“NOL”) and 
6 
the Corporate Alternative Minimum Tax (“CAMT”), (iii) the impact of the 
7 
adjustments to excess ADIT, (iv) the impact of the extension of the temporary 
8 
NYS Tax Rate increase, (v) the impact of the implementation of the IRS 
9 
Revenue Procedure 2023-15, (vi) the impact of a correction to proration on the 
10 
ADIT balances in the Company’s April 28 filing,  and (vii) the impact of 
11 
changes to book plant additions, cost of removal and book depreciation on 
12 
ADIT. 
13 
 
14 
Q. 
How does the update of the ADIT balance from December 31, 2022 to 
15 
March 31, 2023 impact rate base? 
16 
A.  
The actual activity giving rise to ADIT in the period from January 1, 2023 
17 
through March 31, 2023 was higher than estimated in the April 28 filing.  Using 
18 
actual amounts of ADIT increase for the three-month period resulted in a higher 
19 
ADIT, which reduced rate base. 
20 
 
21 


--- Page 26 ---
 
Corrections and Updates Testimony of The Revenue Requirements Panel 
Page 24 of 30 
 
Q. 
How does the revenue requirement increase impact NOL, CAMT, and 
1 
ADIT? 
2 
A. 
The inclusion of the revenue requirement increase in the calculation of the 
3 
Company’s taxable income resulted in a lower amount of NOL carryforward 
4 
generated in the Rate Year through Data Year 3.  The inclusion of the base 
5 
revenue increase in the calculation of the Company’s CAMT, however, resulted 
6 
in a higher amount of CAMT and CAMT carryforward.  Because the deferred 
7 
tax impact of the decrease in NOL carryforward exceeded the deferred tax 
8 
impact of the increase in CAMT carryforward, the inclusion of the base revenue 
9 
increase resulted in higher ADIT, which reduced rate base. 
10 
 
11 
Q. 
How does the adjustment to excess ADIT impact rate base? 
12 
A. 
As the Company returns excess ADIT, the excess ADIT regulatory liability that 
13 
is included in rate base decreases and rate base correspondingly increases.  The 
14 
adjustments made to the amount of the overall excess ADIT regulatory liability 
15 
increased the amount of excess ADIT amortization that flows through the cost 
16 
of service in the Rate Year through Data Year 3.  The increase in the excess 
17 
ADIT amortization, therefore, increased rate base. 
18 
 
19 


--- Page 27 ---
 
Corrections and Updates Testimony of The Revenue Requirements Panel 
Page 25 of 30 
 
Q.  
How does the extension of the NYS Tax Rate increase impact rate base? 
1 
A. 
The extension of the NYS Tax Rate increase through fiscal year 2027 for the 
2 
Company causes the incremental changes in state book-to-tax temporary 
3 
differences that are expected to originate in the Rate Year through Data Year 2 
4 
to be subjected to, and accumulated at, the higher tax rate.  The increased tax 
5 
rate is therefore increasing ADIT, which reduces rate base.  
6 
 
7 
Q. 
Has the IRS implemented any revenue procedures that impact rate base? 
8 
A. 
Yes.  On April 14, 2023, the IRS issued Revenue Procedure 2023-15 (“Rev. 
9 
Proc.”), which outlines a safe harbor method of accounting that taxpayers may 
10 
use to determine whether to deduct or capitalize expenditures to repair, 
11 
maintain, replace, or improve natural gas transmission and distribution 
12 
property. 
13 
 
14 
Q. 
How does the implementation of IRS Revenue Procedure 2023-15 impact 
15 
rate base? 
16 
A. 
While the IRS guidance is complex and requires further analysis, the Company 
17 
made initial estimates of the impact of implementation of the Rev. Proc.  As 
18 
discussed in the response to Information Request No. DPS-425, the Company 
19 
estimated, that to comply with the guidance in Rev. Proc, would cause the 
20 
Company’s gas repairs deductions to decrease by approximately 50 percent.  
21 


--- Page 28 ---
 
Corrections and Updates Testimony of The Revenue Requirements Panel 
Page 26 of 30 
 
The decrease in the annual gas repairs deductions is expected to result in a 
1 
decrease to ADIT.  However, taken in conjunction with the impact of the lower 
2 
gas repairs deduction on the NOL carryforward and CAMT carryforward, the 
3 
implementation of the Rev. Proc. would result in an increase in ADIT in the 
4 
Rate Year and Data Year 1, which decreases rate base, and a decrease in ADIT 
5 
in Data Year 2 and Data Year 3, which increases rate base. 
6 
 
7 
Q. 
Please describe the correction to the proration adjustment for the 
8 
movement in the ADIT balance. 
9 
A. 
In the April 28 filing the Company inadvertently did not apply the proration 
10 
adjustment required in accordance with Section 1.167(1)-1(h)(6) of the federal 
11 
income tax regulations, as was described in the direct testimony.  Following the 
12 
April 28 filing, the Company identified a formula error, whereby the movement 
13 
in the ADIT balance excluding the proration adjustment was used in the 
14 
calculation of rate base.  The Company has remedied the formula error and 
15 
reflected the correct adjustment.  The proration adjustment reduced ADIT, 
16 
which increased rate base. 
17 
 
18

Request for Information 
FROM:
Christopher Logan

National Grid 
SUBJECT: 
Other Benefits Expense 
Request: 
In all interrogatories, all requests for workpapers or supporting calculations shall be construed as 
requesting any Word, Excel or other computer spreadsheet models in original electronic format 
with all formulae intact and unlocked. 
1.
For KEDLI, provide a breakdown of other benefits expenses, by date, by vendor, and by cost
type and cost activity, with the associated dollar amounts for each calendar year, 2018
through 2022.
2.
Referring to the KEDLI Revenue Requirement Panel Testimony on p. 51, in which it states,
"Schedule 15 consists of four pages and presents costs for providing other benefits,
including employee wellness programs and other employee benefits. The Other Benefits
expense is not capitalized largely because of the relatively small dollars associated with this
expense." Provide the following:
a.
A list of all employee wellness programs, and employee benefits allocated to other
benefits expense:
b.
A rationale for why a portion of other benefits expense is not capitalized when
considering the Company's treatment of other relatively small dollar expenses in the
Historic Test Year where costs are being capitalized (e.g., Group Life Insurance).
Response: 
1.
Please see Attachment 1 for a breakdown of other benefits expenses for calendar years 2018
through 2022.  Prior calendar year data represents unadjusted, per-books totals and has not
been normalized.
2.
a.
The Company offers many employee benefit and wellness programs, such as health 
care, life insurance, and thrift plans.  Employee benefit program expenses are 
Exhibit______(RRP-12CU)
Page 1 of 74


--- Page 804 ---
Form 103
quantified in Exhibit __ (RRP-3), Schedules 11 through 18.  The employee benefits 
allocated specifically to Other Benefits expense are shown in Attachment 1 in 
response to Part 1 above and include the ATI Soft Tissue Injury Prevention (“STIP”) 
Program, the Bright Horizons Dependent Care Program, the Virgin Pulse Employee 
Wellness Program, UK to US Cross Charges, and the Appreciate Program.  As noted 
in the response to DPS-258, vendor dollars associated with the Appreciate Program 
(through the vendor “XEXEC LIMITED”) were normalized in the Company’s initial 
filing; however, the accrual entry for December 2022 and the January 2022 reversal 
of the December 2021 accrual will be normalized in the Company’s Corrections and 
Updates filing from Other Benefits and Other Expense, respectively.   
b.
There are capital expenditures associated with Other Benefits.  The testimony
referenced is referring to the burden clearing process for benefits such as health care
and group life insurance, whereby labor benefits are booked to a clearing account
and charged out according to how an employee charges their time, burdening their
labor costs and following the same capital/expense allocations.  Other Benefits
follows a different process because of the nature of the charges.  Specifically, there is
no clearing process for Other Benefits.  Instead, Other Benefits are booked to capital
or operations and maintenance (“O&M”) expense depending on the nature of work
the same as they would be booked to a non-benefit, non-burden cost type (e.g.,
contractors, consultants, etc.).

(through the vendor “XEXEC LIMITED”) were normalized in the Company’s initial 
filing; however, the accrual entry for December 2022 and the January 2022 reversal 
of the December 2021 accrual will be normalized in the Company’s Corrections and 
Updates filing from Other Benefits and Other Expense, respectively.   
b. 
There are capital expenditures associated with Other Benefits.  The testimony 
referenced is referring to the burden clearing process for benefits such as health care 
and group life insurance, whereby labor benefits are booked to a clearing account and 
charged out according to how an employee charges their time, burdening their labor 
costs and following the same capital/expense allocations.  Other Benefits follows a 
different process because of the nature of the charges.  Specifically, there is no 
clearing process for Other Benefits.  Instead, Other Benefits are booked to capital or 
operations and maintenance (“O&M”) expense depending on the nature of work the 
same as they would be booked to a non-benefit, non-burden cost type (e.g., 
contractors, consultants, etc.).

In-Person Events: Costs were forecast using costs developed for a similar program proposed

justice communities to promote clean energy initiatives. The Mass Save program targeted 
environmental justice communities similar to the Disadvantaged Communities the 
Companies are proposing to target for their clean energy programs. 
Localized Social Media Campaigns: Costs were estimated based on the Companies’ 
residential weatherization marketing budget, which planned on spending 50 percent of the

assume paid social media would only be purchased for zip codes whose populations include 
at least 75 percent Disadvantaged Community customers, which is roughly 10 percent.

CommunityFirst Partnership program that aimed to organize events with key community 
organizations in environmental justice communities to promote clean energy initiatives. The 
Mass Save program targeted environmental justice communities similar to the 
Disadvantaged Communities the Companies are proposing to focus on in their service 
territories.

bearing) that reconcile to the EBCAP adjustment of $9.187 million as identified in

Response: 
1.
The Earnings Base Capitalization Adjustment (“EBCAP”) is used to test the reasonableness 
of utility rate base in rate case proceedings and has been applied in New York since the 
1970s. 
The EBCAP adjustment is predicated on the principle that the real measure of the investment 
entitled to earn a fair return is the total capitalization dedicated to public service, as 
represented by the investments of the security holders in the Earnings Base of the utility and 
is not solely the investment in the assets themselves that the utility has dedicated to public 
service. 
Capitalization dedicated to public service is used to fund the Earnings Base, which is 
comprised of the portion of invested capital used to fund the assets required to serve current 
customer needs, (i.e., the rate base) and that portion of invested capital used to fund the assets 
needed to serve future customer needs (i.e., Construction Work in Progress (“CWIP”)).   
Typically, utilities are compensated for the cost of capital supporting the portion of 
capitalization used to fund CWIP through the application of an Allowance for Funds Used 
During Construction (“AFUDC”), leaving the portion of the capitalization supporting the 
rate base to be compensated by current customers through the application of a reasonable 
rate of return on the utility’s rate base.  
Because the total amount of capital dedicated to public service is definite and measurable, 
the amount of the utility’s rate base should not exceed or fall below the total capitalization 
dedicated to public service less the portion of capitalization that is funding the CWIP upon 
which AFUDC is applied.   
The EBCAP adjustment simply measures the difference between the claimed rate base and 
the total capitalization dedicated to public service, less the portion of the earnings base being 
compensated by AFUDC (i.e., the interest bearing CWIP). The claimed rate base is then 
adjusted either up or down to reflect the measurement result. 
Exhibit______(RRP-12CU)
Page 48 of 74


--- Page 851 ---
Form 103
As a general rule, the difference between rate base and earnings base reflects the difference 
in working capital from the 1/8th of O&M expenses included in rate base and the actual 
balance sheet changes included in the earnings base. 
2.
KEDLI’s EBCAP adjustment was a reduction to claimed rate base of $24.379 million for the 
Rate Year ended March 31, 2021 and an increase to claimed rate base of $76.946 million for 
the Rate Year ended March 31, 2022.  The earnings report for the Rate Year ended March 
31, 2023 is not yet available and will be filed by August 31, 2023. 
3.
See Attachment 1 for a detailed Balance Sheet classifying and identifying the specific 
accounts used in determining the EBCAP adjustment of $148.204 million.  A pivot table 
summary is included in Attachment 1 that summarizes the G/L account data by the rate base 
or EBCAP components that can be derived directly from distinct G/L account balances and 
provides references to the specific page and lines where the amounts are presented in 
Exhibit__ (RRP-7), Schedule 6. Note that the presentation of every component of the rate 
base and the EBCAP adjustment cannot be performed directly from balance sheet account 
level detail.  For example,  interest bearing and non-interest bearing CWIP is not recorded 
in distinct G/L accounts.  The application of interest is assigned at the individual 
project/workorder level and must be extracted from PowerPlan, the Company’s Plant 
Accounting subsidiary ledger.  In addition,  there are discrete adjustments to the Plant 
balances to exclude certain projects that are specifically excludable from calculating rate 
base, for example, certain LNG and vaporizer projects.  This detailed information is sourced 
from Plant Accounting’s monthly Net Utility Plant & Depreciation (“NUPD”) capital tracker 
reconciliation, which is used to provide the information necessary to record the monthly 
capital tracker deferral. The summary page from the Historic Test Year End, December 2022 
NUPD reconciliation is presented in Exhibit__ (RRP-7), Schedule 6 as a workpaper to 
support Exhibit__ (RRP-7), Schedule 6 pages 9 and19-21.  A pivot table has been included 
in Attachment 1 to summarize the balances comprising the balance sheet categories of Net 
Utility Plan, CWIP and Accumulated Depreciation that reconcile with the amounts included 
and presented in the NUPD Summary page as presented in Exhibit__ (RRP-7), Schedule 6 
as a workpaper to support pages 9 and 19-21.   Additionally, the rate base also includes 
calculations for Cash Working Capital and Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes (“ADIT”), 
which are not linked directly to balance sheet account detail.  Support for these components

3.    
a. 
The supply cash allowance is a commodity-related cash working capital 
adjustment that is calculated and presented as a normalizing adjustment to the 
Historic Test Year rate base in Exhibit__ (RRP-7) Rate Base Summary.  As 
such, this adjustment’s effect must also be reflected as a normalizing adjustment 
to the calculation of the Historic Test Year EBCAP adjustment presented in 
Exhibit__ (RRP-7), Schedule 6.  Accordingly, the Supply Cash Allowance 
adjustment is not actually removed from the EBCAP adjustment, rather the 
increase in the working capital allowance caused by the Supply Cash Allowance 
normalizing adjustment creates a corresponding increase to the claimed rate base 
(i.e., rate base before the EBCAP adjustment), which results in an equal but 
offsetting effect on the EBCAP adjustment.  The result of which yields no net 
effect to the adjusted rate base (i.e., the rate base after EBCAP adjustment).

SUBJECT:
Allocation of Service Company EV Lease Expenses Allocated to KEDNY and 
KEDLI 
Request: 
In all interrogatories, all requests for workpapers or supporting calculations shall be construed as 
requesting any Word, Excel or other computer spreadsheet models in original electronic format 
with all formulae intact and unlocked. 
The "Inputs and Assumptions" tab of workbooks "RRP-3 OM Sch 24 Transportation NY23" and 
"RRP-3 OM Sch 24 Transportation LI23" lists the allocations of Service Company Electric 
Vehicle (EV) lease expense as 3.69 percent and 2.88 percent, respectively. 
1.  
Explain how the Companies developed these allocation factors. 
 2.  
Explain why such allocation methodology is appropriate for allocating the costs of 
Service Company EVs to KEDNY and KEDLI customers. 
Response: 
1.
Exhibit___(RRP-11), Workpapers to RRP-3, Schedule 24, Workpaper 1 presents total 
Historic Test Year transportation costs originating from the Service Company and the 
proportion of that total charged to each receiving company, resulting in allocations of 
3.69 percent to KEDNY and 2.88 percent to KEDLI.  Please note, however, that these 
rates are presented for informational purposes only and were not used to allocate electric 
vehicle lease costs in the Company’s Rate Year forecast. 
2.
As discussed in the response to part 1, these allocation percentages were not used to 
allocate the lease cost of electric vehicles to KEDNY and KEDLI. Please see 
Exhibit___(RRP-11), Workpaper to Exhibit RRP-3, Schedule 24, Workpaper 5 for the 
allocation of Service Company electric vehicle costs to KEDNY and KEDLI. As shown 
on this workpaper, 100% of the incremental costs for the proposed Service Company 
electric vehicles are allocated to KEDNY and KEDLI and split between the two 
companies using the same ratio that total electric vehicle lease expense is split between 
KEDNY and KEDLI.  
Exhibit______(RRP-12CU)
Page 53 of 74


--- Page 856 ---
Form 103
After further consideration, the Company submits that the better method to allocate the 
Service Company electric vehicle lease expense to KEDNY and KEDLI is by using 
allocation percentages consistent with the approach for allocating costs for the Service 
Company facilities (Melville and Brentwood) at which the electric vehicles will be located. 
As discussed in the Company’s response to DPS-362, parts 6 and 8, National Grid is 
installing four level 2 chargers at the Melville facility, which has an allocation of 31% to 
KEDLI and 54% to KEDNY, and 17 level 2 chargers at the Brentwood facility, with an 
allocation of 97% to KEDLI and 3% to KEDNY. The Company will allocate the Service 
Company electric vehicle lease expense proportionally to KEDNY and KEDLI using these 
ratios, resulting in an allocation of 85% to KEDLI and 15% to KEDNY.  The updated 
allocations will be reflected in the Corrections and Updates filing.

SUBJECT:
Net Operating Loss 
Request: 
In all interrogatories, all requests for workpapers or supporting calculations shall be construed as 
requesting any Word, Excel or other computer spreadsheet models in original electronic format 
with all formulae intact and unlocked. 
For both KEDNY & KEDLI, in reference to p. 116 of the Revenue Requirements Panel's 
testimony, the Companies state "[r]ate base Accumulated Deferred Income Taxes (ADIT) 
includes an asset for Net Operating Loss (NOL) because the Company is estimated to be in a loss 
position. The Company included an estimate of the generation of NOL carryforwards as an 
increase to rate base in each Rate Year and Data Years." 
1.  
Explain what an NOL represents, how it is generated, and the supporting accounting 
transactions. 
2. 
 Explain whether each Company generates the NOL, or if the NOL is generated on a 
consolidated basis. 
3.  
Explain how each Company's customers get the benefit of the NOL. 
4.  
Identify the amount of ADIT associated with the NOL for Rate Year and subsequent Data 
Years. 
5.  
Explain why the NOL creates accumulated deferred tax asset, increasing rate base. 
6.  
Explain why the Company's customers are responsible for paying the deferred taxes 
associated with the NOL. 
7.  
Explain how normalization of the NOL deferred tax asset impacts the income statement, 
and current income tax expense. 
Exhibit______(RRP-12CU)
Page 64 of 74


--- Page 867 ---
Form 103
Response:
1.
A Net Operating Loss (NOL), in a given period, represents an amount by which tax 
deductions reduce an entity’s taxable income below zero. The NOL is generated when an 
entity’s tax-deductible expenses exceed its taxable income in a given period. The amount 
of NOL generated in one period can be carried forward to reduce future taxable income 
and taxes payable. Therefore, the amount of NOL carryforward multiplied by the enacted 
tax rate results in a deferred tax asset. The most significant tax-deductible expenses 
giving rise to the NOL include: accelerated Modified Accelerated Cost Recovery System 
(MACRS) tax depreciation and repairs deductions.
2.
The generation of NOL occurs on a standalone company basis driven by each company’s 
taxable income and tax-deductible expenses.  
3.
The Companies’ customers benefit from the tax-deductible expenses, such as the 
accelerated MACRS tax depreciation and repairs deductions, that reduce the Companies’ 
taxable income and taxes payable. The mechanism by which customers benefit from the 
tax-deductible expenses is the inclusion of the deferred tax liability associated with these 
tax deductions as an offset to rate base. However, the tax-deductible expenses that exceed 
each Company’s taxable income and give rise to the NOL cannot reduce taxes payable 
below zero. Therefore, the portion of the deferred tax liability associated with the tax-
deductible expenses that could not reduce taxes payable below zero (i.e., the portion of 
the tax-deductible expenses that do not provide a cash tax benefit) should not be included 
as an offset to rate base. The measure by which deferred tax liability that offsets the rate 
base needs to be reduced is the deferred tax asset on NOL. The deferred tax asset on NOL 
represents the currently unrealized portion of the tax benefit resulting from tax-
deductible expenses. The inclusion of the deferred tax asset on NOL in rate base properly 
limits customers’ benefit from the deferred tax liability on the tax-deductible expenses to 
that portion of the tax benefit that has been realized. 
4.
In the original rate filing, the Companies generated/(utilized) NOL with the following 
impact within ADIT:
Subsequent to the original submission, a number of changes were made to the   ADIT 
calculation that resulted in the Companies no longer generating federal or state NOL. The 
primary driver of the change in taxable income position from a net operating loss to 
taxable income is a decrease in the estimate of the repairs deduction percentage from 
56.49% to 29.11% for KEDNY and 57.08% to 29.41% for KEDLI. This update, which 
Exhibit______(RRP-12CU)
Page 65 of 74


--- Page 868 ---
Form 103
will be reflected in the Companies’ Corrections and Updates, was made as a result of the 
implementation of the Revenue Procedure 2023-15 issued by the IRS on April 14, 2023, 
which provided new guidance for determining the repairs deduction for natural gas 
transmission and distribution property. Additionally, the taxable income calculation in the 
original filing did not include the impact of the base revenue increase required shown in 
Summary-Rev Rqmt Exh for each rate year. Together the reduction in the repairs 
deduction and the increased income from the base revenue requirement result in the 
Companies no longer generating federal or state NOL. The table below shows the 
updated impact of NOL within ADIT.  
5.
As discussed in the response to question 1 above, the NOL is generated when an entity’s 
tax-deductible expenses exceed its taxable income in a given period. The amount of NOL 
generated in one period can be carried forward to reduce future taxable income and taxes 
payable. Therefore, the amount of NOL carryforward multiplied by the enacted tax rate 
results in a deferred tax asset. The most significant tax-deductible expenses giving rise to 
the NOL include accelerated MACRS tax depreciation and repairs deductions. Because 
the deferred tax liability associated with the accelerated tax deductions is included in rate 
base, the deferred tax asset associated with the resulting NOL similarly needs to be 
included in rate base. Please refer to Attachment 1, Treasury Regulation 1.167(l)-
1(h)(1)(iii), which makes it a normalization violation to exclude the deferred tax asset 
associated with the NOL that resulted from the tax depreciation deductions from rate 
base. 
6.
As discussed in responses to questions 3 and 5 above, customers benefit from the 
inclusion of the deferred tax liability associated with the accelerated tax depreciation and 
repairs deductions in rate base. However, such benefit should be limited to that portion of 
the accelerated tax depreciation and repairs deductions that reduces taxes payable. In the 
case when the accelerated tax depreciation and repairs deductions give rise to the NOL, a 
portion of the tax benefit associated with the deductions that gave rise to the NOL is not 
realized by the Company. Therefore, the deferred tax asset on NOL, which corresponds 
to the unrealized portion of the tax benefit associated with the tax depreciation and 
repairs deductions, serves as a limit on the amount of deferred tax liability included in 
rate base. Excluding deferred tax asset on NOL from rate base would give customers a 
tax benefit, which has not been realized by the Company, leading to a potential 
normalization violation as discussed in response to question 5. 
7.
As illustrated in Attachment 2, when tax-deductible expenses exceed taxable income, the 
Companies’ current tax expense and taxes payable are reduced below zero. This tax 
Exhibit______(RRP-12CU)
Page 66 of 74


--- Page 869 ---
Form 103
benefit, however, can only be realized by the Companies as a reduction in future taxable 
income rather than as a current tax refund claim from a taxing authority. Therefore, the 
Companies are required to establish an NOL carryforward and account for it as a 
reduction to current tax benefit (reducing current tax benefit to zero) and increase in a 
deferred tax benefit (deferred tax asset for NOL). The accounting for NOL has no impact 
on the total tax expense on the income statement, nor the total tax expense recovered 
from the customers as part of the “cost of service.”

Treasury Regulation § 1.167(l)-1 Limitations On Reasonable Allowance In Case Of Property Of
Certain Public Utilities.
1.167(l)-1(h)
Normalization Method Of Accounting--
1.167(l)-1(h)(1)
In General.
1.167(l)-1(h)(1)(i)
— Under section 167(l), a taxpayer uses a normalization method of regulated accounting with respect to public utility
property
1.167(l)-1(h)(1)(i)(a)
— If the same method of depreciation (whether or not a subsection (l) method) is used to compute both its tax
expense and its depreciation expense for purposes of establishing cost of service for ratemaking purposes and for
reflecting operating results in its regulated books of account, and
1.167(l)-1(h)(1)(i)(b)
— If to compute its allowance for depreciation under section 167 it uses a method of depreciation other than the
method it used for purposes described in (a) of this subdivision, the taxpayer makes adjustments consistent with
subparagraph (2) of this paragraph to a reserve to reflect the total amount of the deferral of Federal income tax
liability resulting from the use with respect to all of its public utility property of such different methods of
depreciation.
1.167(l)-1(h)(1)(ii)
— In the case of a taxpayer described in section 167(l) (1) (B) or (2) (C), the reference in subdivision (i) of this
subparagraph shall be a reference only to such taxpayer's “qualified public utility property”. See § 1.167(l)-2(b) for
definition of “qualified public utility property”.
1.167(l)-1(h)(1)(iii)
— Except as provided in this subparagraph, the amount of Federal income tax liability deferred as a result of the use of
different method of depreciation under subdivision (i) of this subparagraph is the excess (computed without regard to
credits) of the amount the tax liability would have been had a subsection (l) method been used over the amount of the
actual tax liability. Such amount shall be taken into account for the taxable year in which such different methods of
depreciation are used. If, however, in respect of any taxable year the use of a method of depreciation other than a
subsection (l) method for purposes of determining the taxpayer's reasonable allowance under section 167(a) results in
a net operating loss carryover (as determined under section 172) to a year succeeding such taxable year which would
not have arisen (or an increase in such carryover which would not have arisen) had the taxpayer determined his
reasonable allowance under section 167(a) using a subsection (l) method, then the amount and time of the deferral of
tax liability shall be taken into account in such appropriate time and manner as is satisfactory to the district director.
